Question
========
Branch prediction is effective when what?


Answerlist
----------
* Fixed function calls
* Branches are unpredictable
* Branches are predictable
* The TLB miss rate is low

Solution
========
The predictor learns from history. It pays off when the branch behaves consistently, for instance a loop that is taken many times in a row. A branch whose outcome looks random cannot be learned and every misprediction flushes the pipeline.

Answerlist
----------
* 0. A direct call is not even a conditional branch to predict.
* 0. This is the worst case: every misprediction costs a pipeline flush.
* 1. A regular, learnable outcome is what makes the predictor accurate.
* 0. The TLB is unrelated to branch prediction.
